newsitem.title: UK: Brown says made considerable UK fiscal tightening.
newsitem.headline: Brown says made considerable UK fiscal tightening.

text.p: British Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown said his first budget represented a considerable fiscal tightening and helped to bring monetary and fiscal policy into balance.
In an interview with BBC radio, he said he had had to cool the economy down with an interest rate increase immediately after coming into office.
"What I've now done in this budget is get the fiscal policy sorted out," Brown said.
"When you look at the figures ...in detail, you'll see it's a very considerable fiscal tightening. We are reducing the deficit year on year. We are doing it over a period of five years."
Asked what he had done to dampen consumer spending, Brown cited two measures in the housing market -- curbing mortgage interest tax relief and raising stamp duty on more expensive properties.
"I think people, when they look at this in detail, will see that I've been tough."
Brown said he believed he had got the balance right, not just for a year or two but over five years.
"I have taken action in the budget to bring monetary and fiscal policy back into balance," he added.
